rationale: The child establishes when competitive-status employees occupying excepted positions receive protection against separation. C23 is the strongest thematic candidate because it addresses acquisition of competitive status and related personnel rights, but its Foreign Service reinstatement machinery and operative provisions are materially different. C12 and C08 also concern federal reemployment and Civil Service Commission authority, yet neither contains the child's distinction between confidential or policy-determining positions and other Schedule A or B positions, nor its separation-protection mechanism. The overlap consists of general civil-service terminology and routine grants of Commission authority, insufficient to show a reusable drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whenever any position in Schedule A or B ... is occupied by a person having a competitive status
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Any officer or employee ... shall be considered as having a competitive status
shared_material.explanation: C23 shares the term “competitive status,” but applies it to acquiring status during Foreign Service assignments rather than separation protections for employees in excepted positions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Commission shall designate such positions in Schedules A and B
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Civil Service Commission is authorized ... to prescribe such rules and regulations as may be necessary
shared_material.explanation: C23 gives the Commission administrative authority, but this is routine machinery and does not reproduce the child's position-designation test.

shared_material.child_excerpt: he shall be separated therefrom only in accordance with the provisions of this order and the Civil Service Rules and Regulations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Commission may issue such regulations or instructions as it may deem necessary or appropriate for carrying out the said reemployment provisions.
shared_material.explanation: C08 similarly invokes Commission regulations, but only for statutory reemployment provisions; the language and substantive mechanism are not materially parallel.
